## Introduction

In an affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) experiment, a tagged
protein, the *bait*, is purified from cell lysate together with the proteins
bound to it, and mass spectrometry identifies and quantifies these *preys*.
Most preys in a purification are not genuine interaction partners: abundant
proteins, proteins binding the beads or the tag, and carry-over appear in
almost every purification. Negative-control purifications, without the bait or
with the tag alone, show what this background looks like.

SAINT (Significance Analysis of INTeractome, Choi et al. 2011) scores each
bait-prey pair. It models the abundance of a prey in the purifications of a
bait as coming either from a true interaction or from the background, estimates
the background distribution of each prey from the negative controls, and
returns the probability that the interaction is true (`AvgP`) and a Bayesian
false discovery rate (`BFDR`). SAINTexpress (Teo et al. 2014) is the faster,
simplified implementation of SAINT. It has a model for spectral counts and one
for intensities, and can use known prey-prey interactions as a prior.

Use SAINT when you have AP-MS (or proximity labelling) data with negative
controls and want to separate interaction partners of each bait from
background, for example to filter interactions at `BFDR <= 0.05` before
building a network. SAINT does not compare abundances between conditions;
that is a differential-expression question.

SAINTexpress has so far been available as a C++ program, run outside R on
text files. saintexpress implements both of its models in R, so interaction
scoring can be part of an R analysis, run on every platform, and start from
data already held in Bioconductor containers. The scores agree with the
native SAINTexpress 3.6.3 program (see below).

Related Bioconductor packages:

- **artMS** converts MaxQuant results into the input files of SAINTexpress
  (`artmsEvidenceToSaintExpress()`); the scoring itself then needs the native
  program. saintexpress can score these tables directly in R.
- **apComplex** estimates protein complex membership, as a bipartite graph of
  proteins and complexes, from bait-prey observations. It answers a different
  question: which proteins form complexes, rather than how likely each single
  bait-prey interaction is. Interactions filtered by SAINT can be its input.

## The TIP49 data

saintexpress ships a subset of the example data of SAINTexpress, an AP-MS
experiment on human protein complexes containing TIP49a/TIP49b (RUVBL1/RUVBL2)
with spectral counts (Sardiu et al. 2008). The subset keeps 4 baits (ACTR8,
ZNHIT1, INO80B, VPS72) in 7 purifications, all 9 negative controls, and the 78
preys seen in at least 3 bait purifications (`inst/scripts/tip49.md`). The
files are the headerless tables native SAINTexpress reads.

```{r tip49}
library(saintexpress)
tip49 <- system.file("extdata", "tip49", package = "saintexpress")
read_dat <- function(file) {
  read.delim(file.path(tip49, file), header = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
si <- list(
  inter = read_dat("inter.dat"),
  prey = read_dat("prey.dat"),
  bait = read_dat("bait.dat")
)
lapply(si, head, 3)
```

`run_saint()` takes a list of three data frames. Their columns are matched by
name when all required names are present, otherwise by position, as here.

| Table | Column | Type | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inter` | `ipId` | character | Purification (IP) |
| | `baitId` | character | Bait of the IP |
| | `preyId` | character | Prey |
| | `quant` | numeric | Spectral count (whole number >= 0) or intensity (> 0) |
| `prey` | `preyId` | character | Prey, unique |
| | `preyLength` | numeric | Protein length (optional, not used) |
| | `preyGeneId` | character | Gene name (optional, defaults to `preyId`) |
| `bait` | `ipId` | character | Purification, unique |
| | `baitId` | character | Bait; replicate IPs share it |
| | `CorT` | character | `T` for a bait IP, `C` for a negative control |

`validate_saint_input()` checks the tables. If it passes, `run_saint()`
accepts them; otherwise it names the table and column at fault.

```{r validate}
validate_saint_input(si, mode = "spc")
```

## Spectral-count scoring

```{r score-spc}
scores <- run_saint(si, mode = "spc")
dim(scores)
names(scores)
```

Each row is a bait-prey pair. The columns follow the native `list.txt`:

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| `Spec`, `SpecSum`, `AvgSpec`, `NumReplicates` | Prey counts in the replicate IPs of the bait, their sum and mean, number of replicates |
| `ctrlCounts` | Prey counts in the control IPs |
| `AvgP`, `MaxP` | Probability of a true interaction, averaged over replicates and the highest one |
| `TopoAvgP`, `TopoMaxP`, `SaintScore`, `boosted_by` | Scores with the prey-prey prior (see below) |
| `logOddsScore` | Lowest replicate log odds of true vs background |
| `FoldChange` | Mean count divided by the background mean |
| `BFDR` | Bayesian false discovery rate |

The highest-scoring preys of the bait ZNHIT1 include the other subunits of the
SRCAP chromatin-remodelling complex it belongs to, such as SRCAP, ACTR6, DMAP1,
RUVBL1, RUVBL2, YEATS4 and VPS72, all absent or nearly absent from the
controls:

```{r top-hits}
znhit1 <- scores[scores$Bait == "ZNHIT1", ]
head(znhit1[order(-znhit1$AvgP, -znhit1$FoldChange),
            c("Prey", "Spec", "ctrlCounts", "AvgP", "FoldChange", "BFDR")], 10)
```

At a Bayesian FDR of 5%:

```{r hits}
hits <- scores[scores$BFDR <= 0.05, ]
nrow(hits)
head(sort(table(hits$Bait), decreasing = TRUE))
```

```{r volcano, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5}
is_hit <- scores$BFDR <= 0.05
plot(
  log2(scores$FoldChange), scores$AvgP,
  pch = 19, cex = 0.5,
  col = ifelse(is_hit, "#B23A48", "#3D6F9966"),
  xlab = "log2 fold change over background", ylab = "AvgP",
  main = "TIP49 subset, spectral counts"
)
legend("bottomright", legend = c("BFDR <= 0.05", "other"),
       col = c("#B23A48", "#3D6F99"), pch = 19, bty = "n")
```

## Intensity scoring

`mode = "int"` uses the SAINTexpress intensity model: intensities are log
transformed and standardised, and both the true and the background
distribution are normal. Here the TIP49 counts stand in for intensities, as in
the SAINTexpress example.

```{r score-int}
scores_int <- run_saint(si, mode = "int")
head(scores_int[order(-scores_int$AvgP),
                c("Bait", "Prey", "AvgIntensity", "AvgP", "BFDR")])
```

## Agreement with native SAINTexpress

`inst/extdata/tip49` also holds the `list.txt` files written by the native
SAINTexpress 3.6.3 programs for these inputs (`inst/scripts/tip49.md` describes
how). The R scores agree with them; the package tests check this for both
models and both optimizers.

```{r native}
native_diff <- function(r_scores, file) {
  native <- read.delim(file.path(tip49, file), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  both <- merge(native, r_scores, by = c("Bait", "Prey"), suffixes = c("_native", "_r"))
  vapply(c("AvgP", "MaxP", "SaintScore", "BFDR"), function(column) {
    max(abs(both[[paste0(column, "_native")]] - both[[paste0(column, "_r")]]))
  }, numeric(1))
}
rbind(
  spc = native_diff(scores, "list_spc.txt"),
  int = native_diff(scores_int, "list_int.txt")
)
```

The spectral-count scores match the native output exactly (both are rounded
to two decimals). The intensity scores differ by a few thousandths in the
probabilities and by up to 0.02 in BFDR, from small numerical differences
between the two implementations of the intensity model.

## Optimizer and tuning arguments

**`optimizer`**. The model parameters are fitted by maximum likelihood.
`"base"` (default) uses `stats::optim()` with method L-BFGS-B. `"nloptr"`
uses the COBYLA algorithm of the NLopt library, like native SAINTexpress, and
needs the nloptr package. Both give nearly the same scores:

```{r optimizer}
if (requireNamespace("nloptr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  scores_nloptr <- run_saint(si, mode = "spc", optimizer = "nloptr")
  max(abs(scores_nloptr$AvgP - scores$AvgP))
}
```

**`R`** (default 100) is the most replicates averaged into `AvgP`: with
`R = 1`, `AvgP` is the probability of the best replicate, equal to `MaxP`.
This rewards interactions seen strongly in a single replicate.

```{r arg-R}
scores_r1 <- run_saint(si, mode = "spc", R = 1)
all(scores_r1$AvgP == scores_r1$MaxP)
c(default = sum(scores$BFDR <= 0.05), R1 = sum(scores_r1$BFDR <= 0.05))
```

**`L`** (default 100, spectral counts only) is the number of control IPs used
for the background of each prey: for every prey the `L` controls with the
highest counts are taken. A smaller `L` makes the background stricter when
some controls are much cleaner than others. TIP49 has 9 controls, so the
default uses all of them.

```{r arg-L}
scores_l4 <- run_saint(si, mode = "spc", L = 4)
c(default = sum(scores$BFDR <= 0.05), L4 = sum(scores_l4$BFDR <= 0.05))
```

**`p2p_mapping`** gives known prey-prey interactions, for example from
protein complex databases. A prey whose known partners are also detected with
the bait gets a higher topology score `TopoAvgP`; `SaintScore` is the larger
of `AvgP` and `TopoAvgP`, and `boosted_by` lists the partners. The mapping is
a list with one element per row of the prey table, holding the row numbers of
the linked preys. Here, members of the INO80 and SRCAP complexes are linked:

```{r p2p}
complexes <- list(
  INO80 = c("RUVBL1", "RUVBL2", "ACTR5", "ACTR8", "INO80B", "INO80C", "INO80D",
            "INO80E", "NFRKB", "TFPT", "MCRS1", "UCHL5", "YY1", "ACTL6A"),
  SRCAP = c("SRCAP", "ZNHIT1", "VPS72", "H2AFZ", "DMAP1", "ACTL6A", "RUVBL1",
            "RUVBL2")
)
prey_ids <- si$prey[[1]]
p2p_mapping <- lapply(prey_ids, function(prey) {
  partners <- unlist(complexes[vapply(complexes, function(x) prey %in% x, logical(1))])
  match(setdiff(unique(partners), prey), prey_ids)
})
scores_topo <- run_saint(si, mode = "spc", p2p_mapping = p2p_mapping)
boosted <- scores_topo[scores_topo$TopoAvgP > scores_topo$AvgP, ]
head(boosted[, c("Bait", "Prey", "AvgP", "TopoAvgP", "SaintScore", "boosted_by")])
```

## Data in ExpressionSet, SummarizedExperiment, QFeatures or anndataR

Quantitative proteomics data are often held in a container: an
`ExpressionSet`, a `SummarizedExperiment`, an assay of a `QFeatures` object,
or an `anndataR` object when data are exchanged with Python. saintexpress
depends on none of them. Each holds the three pieces `run_saint()` needs:

| Piece | ExpressionSet | SummarizedExperiment, QFeatures assay | anndataR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quantity matrix, preys x IPs | `exprs(eset)` | `assay(se)` | `t(adata$X)` |
| Sample table, one row per IP | `pData(eset)` | `colData(se)` | `adata$obs` |
| Feature table, one row per prey | `fData(eset)` | `rowData(se)` | `adata$var` |

The function below scores an `ExpressionSet` and returns the scores as an
`ExpressionSet` with preys in rows and baits in columns: `exprs()` holds
`AvgP`, and `MaxP`, `SaintScore`, `FoldChange` and `BFDR` are further assay
data elements. It needs the Biobase package.

```{r eset-wrapper, eval = requireNamespace("Biobase", quietly = TRUE)}
run_saint_eset <- function(eset, bait = "bait", cort = "CorT",
                           mode = "spc", ...) {
  quant <- Biobase::exprs(eset)
  samples <- Biobase::pData(eset)
  detected <- which(!is.na(quant) & quant > 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
  si <- list(
    inter = data.frame(
      ipId = colnames(quant)[detected[, 2]],
      baitId = samples[[bait]][detected[, 2]],
      preyId = rownames(quant)[detected[, 1]],
      quant = quant[detected]
    ),
    prey = data.frame(preyId = rownames(quant)),
    bait = data.frame(ipId = colnames(quant), baitId = samples[[bait]],
                      CorT = samples[[cort]])
  )
  scores <- run_saint(si, mode = mode, ...)

  baits <- sort(unique(scores$Bait))
  cell <- cbind(match(scores$Prey, rownames(quant)), match(scores$Bait, baits))
  to_matrix <- function(column) {
    m <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(quant), length(baits),
                dimnames = list(rownames(quant), baits))
    m[cell] <- scores[[column]]
    m
  }
  Biobase::ExpressionSet(
    assayData = Biobase::assayDataNew(
      exprs = to_matrix("AvgP"),
      MaxP = to_matrix("MaxP"),
      SaintScore = to_matrix("SaintScore"),
      FoldChange = to_matrix("FoldChange"),
      BFDR = to_matrix("BFDR")
    ),
    phenoData = Biobase::AnnotatedDataFrame(
      data.frame(bait = baits, row.names = baits)
    ),
    featureData = Biobase::featureData(eset)
  )
}
```

We put the TIP49 counts into an `ExpressionSet` and score it:

```{r eset-run, eval = requireNamespace("Biobase", quietly = TRUE)}
counts <- tapply(
  si$inter[[4]],
  list(factor(si$inter[[3]], levels = si$prey[[1]]),
       factor(si$inter[[1]], levels = si$bait[[1]])),
  sum
)
eset <- Biobase::ExpressionSet(
  counts,
  phenoData = Biobase::AnnotatedDataFrame(
    data.frame(bait = si$bait[[2]], CorT = si$bait[[3]],
               row.names = si$bait[[1]])
  )
)
eset

scores_eset <- run_saint_eset(eset)
scores_eset
Biobase::assayDataElement(scores_eset, "BFDR")[c("RUVBL1", "RUVBL2", "SRCAP"), ]
```

A `SummarizedExperiment`, or an assay of a `QFeatures` object, converts to an
`ExpressionSet` with the coercion that the SummarizedExperiment package
provides:

```{r se-to-eset, eval = FALSE}
scores_se <- run_saint_eset(as(se, "ExpressionSet"))
```
